title: Blambangan Kingdom
capsule: Blambangan was a Hindu-influenced kingdom at the eastern tip of Java, in the region of modern Banyuwangi, that survived as the last major Hindu polity on Java after the collapse of Majapahit, sustained by its geographic isolation and close cultural and dynastic ties with Hindu Bali across the narrow strait. Its most powerful ruler, Tawang Alun II (r. 1655–1691), extended the kingdom westward toward Jember and Lumajang while repeatedly resisting the Islamizing pressure of the Mataram Sultanate, often with Balinese support. Succession disputes in the early eighteenth century left Blambangan fractured and contested between Balinese overlords, Mataram's successors, and the encroaching Dutch East India Company (VOC), whose growing interference set the stage for the kingdom's loss of independence by the mid-eighteenth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Blambangan's territorial extent is broadly documented in Dutch VOC records and Balinese chronicle traditions, but the precise northern and western frontiers with Mataram and later Dutch territories shifted substantially across the period.
